Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0003] Handle the empty/zero-denominator case explicitly: The accepted implementation returns ZERO when total quantity is zero, avoiding a division-by-zero for invoices without lines.
  For weighted-average or ratio computations, sum the denominator first and return the module's zero constant when it is zero, rather than relying on the caller or catching exceptions.
- [rb-0001] Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected because the team requires ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent).
  Before returning any monetary Decimal, check the repo's money module for a rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and wrap the final value with it. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module and existing helpers before implementing: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py revealed ZERO, to_money, and round_money, which the accepted solution reused instead of raw arithmetic.
  When a task involves amounts, open the money/utility module first and reuse its constants and converters (ZERO, to_money, round_money) so behavior matches the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Match existing error codes and validation style before writing new code
item.description: Grep the codebase for BillingError usages and isinstance checks to mirror established conventions rather than inventing new ones.
item.content: Before implementing validation, search sibling modules for existing error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and type-check patterns. Reusing the same codes and message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on error codes.

item.title: Guard against bool passing isinstance(x, int)
item.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so quantity validation must explicitly reject booleans.
item.content: When validating an integer parameter, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before range checks; otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and corrupt data.

item.title: Normalize money through the project's helpers before comparing
item.description: Convert and round unit_price via to_money/round_money before the negativity check so comparisons use the canonical Decimal form.
item.content: Raw inputs may be strings, ints, or Decimals; passing them through the module's to_money and round_money helpers first ensures the negative check and stored value are consistent and reject floats per existing policy.
